comment_data.body:
This seems worth coming back to. It's a bug that doesn't seem so unlikely to occur in practice and that is difficult for users to work around.

PR https://github.com/cython/cython/pull/7681 has a short reproducer although not quite the right fix yet.

> [...] although not quite the right fix yet.

It isn't a "wrong" fix as such.

Just to give a few more details. I think really it should be fixed in

https://github.com/cython/cython/blob/258b71013208108bb59c8c696430bf4770d547ad/Cython/Compiler/PyrexTypes.py#L4738

so that if you have `vector[T]` then you specialize that to `vector[U]` then specialize that to `vector[int]` it ends up being the same as if you have `vector[T]` and specialize it directly to `vector[int]`

The difficulty that I didn't manage to solve when I last looked at it was

https://github.com/cython/cython/blob/258b71013208108bb59c8c696430bf4770d547ad/Cython/Compiler/PyrexTypes.py#L4749-L4750

I can't remember all the details right now but the recursive template types are quite difficult to deal with and relatively common pattern in C++.

-----------------------------------------

My view is that the fix in https://github.com/cython/cython/pull/7681 should be included because it is the right thing to do. But feels like it coincidentally fixes the issue rather than convincingly fixes the issue. But we could merge it and leave the "real" problem as an open issue to fix. We wouldn't want to revert the fix there anyway.

Hmm, right. Utility code is a module global thing, so local directives should always be irrelevant (or at least be ignored).
Should we generally replace the local directives with the global directives when generating Cython utility code?
We could probably avoid the `compiler_directives` option for `CythonUtilityCode` all together and just allow explicit overrides if we need it for specific code. The global directives can just be read from the current module.
I'll prepare something. That seems a change that should go into a fresh x.y release.

>  Should we generally replace the local directives with the global directives when generating Cython utility code?

For most utility code, I think at least global directives, and possibly always default directives (i.e. I'm not necessarily sure why most of them need to be overrideable).

That might need to vary a bit for things like properties of cdef classes. Although those are usually generated by a different mechanism anyway.

milestone.description:
Main features:
- Pattern matching
- Generics / subscripted container types
- `@cython.collection_type()`
- `restrict`
- more vectorcalls
- more thread safety
- smaller modules, more shared code
- remove Py3.8 support, keep Py3.9+
